newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - SE Asian prices mixed as inquiries rise.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - SE Asian prices mixed as inquiries rise.

text.p: Southeast Asian rubber prices are expected to firm up this week on rising demand, some regional dealers said on Monday, but others remained cautious and said they believed prices would be stuck in a range.
"Prices should jump five to 10 percent across the board next week if the weather stays wet and demand returns," a trader in Kuala Lumpur said.
But Singapore-based rubber dealers were wary, saying prices will remain range-bound this week.
"A lot of buyers will make inquiries, but they won't buy rubber every day. It's still going to stay within a range," a buyer in one Western company here said.

One Indonesian trader in the north Sumatran city of Medan said his company had received a rising number of purchases nquiries from the United States and Europe and that he hoped to strike some significant deals next week.

"The major consumers are all making inquiries, but they are still not coming in to buy," a senior Singapore-based trader said. "Unless that happens, prices will be range-bound despite the slight increases in prices we've recently seen."
Another factor that may inhibit the market is the high level of stocks in Japan, which have recently capped any surge in Japanese prices, dealers said.
"Any upswing in Tokyo and Kobe has been capped by the high stocks there, discouraging potential buyers," one dealer said.

Indonesian dealers said SIR20 offer prices for December/January deliveries were likely to be between 56.00-56.50 U.S. cents/lb FOB Medan and between 55.50-56.00 cents FOB Padang, Palembang and Surabaya, and at 55.25-55.75 cents FOB Jambi and Pontianak.
One Jakarta dealer said RSS1 prices were also likely to stay steady in the coming days due to expected ample demand.
He said RSS1 was last sold at 125.50 cents/kg FOB Semarang for December deliveries to Europe against the previous 123 cents/kg.
An Indonesian latex dealer said prices were likely to remain stable despite expected lower supplies following the recent loading of a large quantity of latex in Medan.
Traded prices for high amoniac grade latex, with 60 percent dry rubber content, are expected to hold around 2,200 rupiah/kg for November deliveries.
Malaysian traders said they expected rubber prices to go up if the rains continue in the northern growing areas and buying interest returns.
"We've come down so low that there will be a sharp jump once the market recovers," a Malaysian trader said.

The December buying price for RSS1 was quoted by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board at 317.50 Malaysian cents a kg at the close of the market on Friday. SMR20 for November buyer was quoted at 311 cents.
The two grades have been trading in a tight range since September after an active round of short-covering by European, Chinese and Middle East buyers.
Prices received a boost on Thursday when Australians and South Koreans emerged in late trading to do some light covering for SMR20.
Dealers said demand for latex was also soft but supply was tighter after recent rains. Drum latex was offered at 234 Malaysian cents a kg by traders at the close of last week.
Thai rubber prices were mostly steady to firmer as rains hampered tapping and supplies tightened, trade sources said.
There have been some inquiries from both Japan and China but the actual demand remained weak, they said.
"There was some buying, but more of inquiries from countries in the Far East," one trader said. "But prices seemed to be supported by tighter supplies rather than demand."
Thai benchmark RSS3 for December shipment was quoted around US$1.23-$1.25 a kg FOB Bangkok at the end of last week against $1.22-$1.24 a kg the previous week.
STR20 was quoted around $1.22 a kg. The latex price was steady at 95 U.S. cents a kg FOB Bangkok.
(With contributions from Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia)
- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
